findings: artifacts/selected.json and artifacts/contract.json contradict each other on washer damage: the selected specification caps fracture/permanent-deformation outcomes at 0.40, while the contract makes both native JOINT_BREAK and its residual-based damage proxy permanent hard-zero failures. The current revision requires hard zero for actual JOINT_BREAK and says constraint residual must not be represented as real plastic deformation; reconcile the selected specification and separately name/justify any residual-based failure.

The contract's direct-contact provenance rule makes any GR–M or GR–WS contact lasting 12 physics intervals (0.05 s) an immutable hard-zero failure, even without removal, support, loss, damage, or a shortcut. This conflicts with selected.json, which prohibits deliberate workpiece removal, and with the requirement that arbitrary contact/impulse windows not disqualify a physically safe valid outcome. Grade an observable shortcut or harmful outcome instead, or provide a non-arbitrary physical predicate.

The stated score arithmetic is otherwise internally consistent across all required controls: initial 0; complete loading 0.20; half recovery 0.20+0.70*(0.5/0.98)=0.5571428571; threshold recovery 0.90; full dwell 1.00; every declared hard failure gives 0. Timeout processing is also consistent: 4800 controls at 20 Hz equals 240 s and 57,600 production intervals at 240 Hz; Q from O_56880 through O_57600 spans 720 completed intervals, while 719 intervals leaves 0.90. Physics-substep observables, 20 Hz reporting, and the separate 480 Hz refinement run are distinguished explicitly.
